key_finding: Lead-vs-co-movement verdict: contemporaneous daily corr(SOX,SPY)=0.71 is shared beta, NOT a forecast. Bidirectional Granger (both directions significant) — feedback, not clean lead. Toda-Yamamoto SOX->SPY sig lags [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 21], reverse [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 21]. Relative-strength incremental edge over SPY-own-momentum at some horizon = True. Winner (rs_mom6m/P1_long_cash pro/L63/LB63): OOS Sharpe 1.57 vs B&H 0.82 (beats=True) and vs SPY-own-momentum 0.83 (beats=True). Winner beats SPY-own-momentum but with a strong overfit signature (IS Sharpe 0.10 vs OOS 1.57; median valid combo 0.67 below B&H; loses in all pre-OOS crises). Granger is bidirectional (feedback), not a clean lead. bootstrap p=0.041, durability 'conditionally_durable', rolling-corr 'sign_unstable'.
mechanism: Semiconductors (SOX) and SPY are both high-beta equity indices that co-move ~71% daily — shared market beta, not a forecast. The tradable signal is SOX/SPY relative-strength 6-month momentum, which partials out the common beta and asks whether chips are leading or lagging. Causality is bidirectional feedback (Toda-Yamamoto significant SOX->SPY and SPY->SOX at all lags), not a clean semiconductor lead. The weak forward edge (R²~1%) adds over SPY's own momentum only marginally and horizon-dependently (21d p=0.033; not 63d p=0.075). Winner: long SPY when lagged rel-strength momentum is above its rolling 75th percentile, else cash; procyclical.
caveats: IS Sharpe 0.10 vs OOS 1.57 — the 2021-06 to 2026-06 OOS window was a favorable semiconductor bull, not a representative draw.
Median valid tournament combo (0.67) underperforms buy&hold (0.82): the search mostly found losers; the winner is plausibly the luckiest of 4,607 tries. Win-rate 0.20.
The rule LOST in every pre-OOS crisis: Dot-Com Sharpe -1.16, GFC -1.06, COVID -0.95.
Bootstrap p=0.041 (marginal). Rolling-corr sign stability 0.42 (sign_unstable). No structural break (sup-F p=0.665). No final exam yet.
Edge over SPY-own-momentum is marginal and horizon-dependent: adds at 21d (p=0.033), not at 63d (p=0.075); incremental R² ~1%.
Causality is bidirectional feedback, not a clean SOX->SPY lead. The 0.709 daily corr is co-movement (shared beta), not a forecast.
Drawdown improvement (-9.7% vs -24.5%) is real but regime-shaped, not a tested all-weather property.
narrative_summary: SOX/SPY relative-strength momentum beat both buy&hold and a SPY-own-momentum benchmark on OOS Sharpe (1.57 vs 0.82 and 0.83), but the win rests on a benign semis-bull window and shows a strong overfit signature. The honest story is co-movement (not a lead), bidirectional feedback (not causation), and a thin, horizon-dependent edge — a fragile hypothesis pending a frozen final exam.
